comment: One symbol key per formula, used everywhere a formula is displayed: module cheat sheets, the mock formulae panels, the exam reference sheet, flashcards and the Priority Module. Keyed by the formula text exactly as authored (whitespace-normalised at match time). 'skip' marks entries that are not formulas and need no key. The injector reports anything unmatched, so coverage is provable rather than assumed.

glossary.average speed = distance moved ÷ time ta: average speed in m/s · distance moved in m · time taken in s
glossary.a = (v − u) ÷ t: a = acceleration (m/s²) · v = final velocity (m/s) · u = initial velocity (m/s) · t = time taken (s)
glossary.F = m × a: F = resultant force (N) · m = mass (kg) · a = acceleration (m/s²)
glossary.W = m × g: W = weight, the gravitational force (N) · m = mass (kg) · g = gravitational field strength (N/kg — numerically the same as acceleration in m/s²; use 10)
glossary.moment = force × perpendicular distance: moment in N m · force in N · perpendicular distance in m — convert cm to m before substituting
glossary.v² = u² + (2 × a × s): v = final speed (m/s) · u = initial speed (m/s) · a = acceleration (m/s²) · s = distance moved (m)
glossary.ρ = m ÷ V: ρ (rho) = density (kg/m³, or g/cm³) · m = mass (kg, or g) · V = volume (m³, or cm³) — 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³
glossary.P = F ÷ A: P = pressure (Pa, which is N/m²) · F = force (N) · A = area (m²)
glossary.ΔP = h × g × ρ: ΔP = pressure difference (Pa) · h = depth (m) · g = gravitational field strength (N/kg) · ρ = density of the fluid (kg/m³)
glossary.ΔQ = m × c × ΔT: ΔQ = energy transferred (J) · m = mass (kg — convert grams first) · c = specific heat capacity (J/kg °C) · ΔT = temperature change (°C)
glossary.p₁ × V₁ = p₂ × V₂: p₁, V₁ = pressure and volume before · p₂, V₂ = after · pressure in Pa or kPa, volume in m³ or cm³ — any units, provided both sides match · temperature must stay constant
glossary.p₁ ÷ T₁ = p₂ ÷ T₂: p₁, T₁ = pressure and temperature before · p₂, T₂ = after · pressure in Pa or kPa · T must be in kelvin (K), never °C · volume must stay constant
glossary.K = °C + 273 °C = K − 273: K = temperature in kelvin · °C = temperature in degrees Celsius · absolute zero is 0 K = −273 °C
glossary.V = I × R: V = voltage, or potential difference (V) · I = current (A) · R = resistance (Ω, ohms)
glossary.Q = I × t: Q = charge (C, coulombs) · I = current (A) · t = time (s)
glossary.P = I × V: P = power (W, watts) · I = current (A) · V = voltage (V)
glossary.E = Q × V: E = energy transferred (J) · Q = charge (C) · V = voltage (V)
glossary.E = I × V × t: E = energy transferred (J) · I = current (A) · V = voltage (V) · t = time (s — convert minutes first)
glossary.v = f × λ: v = wave speed (m/s) · f = frequency (Hz — convert kHz to Hz first) · λ (lambda) = wavelength (m)
glossary.f = 1 ÷ T: f = frequency (Hz) · T = time period, the time for one complete wave (s)
glossary.W = F × d: W = work done (J) · F = force (N) · d = distance moved in the direction of the force (m)
glossary.GPE = m × g × h: GPE = gravitational potential energy (J) · m = mass (kg) · g = gravitational field strength (N/kg; use 10) · h = change in height (m)
glossary.KE = ½ × m × v²: KE = kinetic energy (J) · m = mass (kg) · v = speed (m/s) — the speed is squared, so doubling it quadruples the energy
glossary.efficiency = (useful energy output ÷ tot: both energies in J · the answer is a percentage · it must be useful energy OUTPUT over total energy INPUT — dropping either word loses the mark
glossary.P = W ÷ t: P = power (W, watts) · W = work done, or energy transferred (J) · t = time taken (s) — one watt is one joule per second
glossary.m × g × h = ½ × m × v²: m = mass (kg) · g = gravitational field strength (N/kg) · h = height fallen (m) · v = speed at the bottom (m/s) — the mass cancels, so the speed does not depend on it
glossary.²³⁸₉₂U → ²³⁴₉₀Th + ⁴₂He: top number = mass number (protons + neutrons) · bottom number = atomic number (protons) · ⁴₂He is the alpha particle · mass drops by 4, atomic number by 2
glossary.¹⁴₆C → ¹⁴₇N + ⁰₋₁e: top number = mass number (protons + neutrons) · bottom number = atomic number (protons) · ⁰₋₁e is the beta particle, an electron from the nucleus · mass unchanged, atomic number up 1
glossary.v = (2 × π × r) ÷ T: v = orbital speed (m/s) · r = orbital radius (m) · T = time for one full orbit (s)
glossary.p₁V₁ = p₂V₂: p₁, V₁ = pressure and volume before · p₂, V₂ = after · temperature constant · any units, provided both sides match
glossary.F = (mv − mu) ÷ t: F = force (N) · m = mass (kg) · v = final velocity (m/s) · u = initial velocity (m/s) · t = time (s) — mv − mu is the change in momentum (kg m/s)
glossary.¹⁴₆C → ___ ___N + ⁰₋₁e: top number = mass number (protons + neutrons) · bottom number = atomic number (protons) · ⁰₋₁e is the beta particle · both sides must balance: mass numbers total the same, atomic numbers total the same
